findings.basis: AOSP CarrierConfig assets in this tree: carrier id 1839 Verizon Wireless (lines 82-85) and the Xfinity Mobile ids 2032 and 2556 carry exactly ['*71','*72']. Google's CarrierSettings carry the same value for Fi Extended (GrapheneOS Pixel CarrierSettings snapshot, gid1-matched Fi entries, Pixel firmware CP3A.261005.005), for Spectrum Us on 314-020 and for Verizononsitelte Us on 999-480 (Pixel vendor CarrierSettings bundles). For 310-012 the Google lane already serves ['*71','*72'] from one of its two entries. These are real carrier settings of Verizon-network operators. The Fi Extended source entries are gid1-specific while the OCD profiles name single networks; that is a matching question with no emergency effect for this value.
findings.effect: blockCallForwardingNumberWhileRoaming (TelephonyConnectionService.java:2153-2186) runs from getTelephonyConnection (1735-1742) for every outgoing call, emergency calls included: placeEmergencyConnection calls getTelephonyConnection with isEmergencyNumber=true (2726-2731) and the check has no emergency exception. It blocks only when ServiceState reports roaming, the phone is not using IMS for voice (with support_ims_call_forwarding_while_roaming_bool at its default true, VoLTE or Wi-Fi calling enabled and IMS in service turns the check off), and the dialled string starts with a listed prefix. Then the call fails at once with DIALED_CALL_FORWARDING_WHILE_ROAMING (Telecom ERROR with a message). The default is null, which blocks nothing (CarrierConfigManager.java:12172). With ['*71','*72'] only dialled strings that begin with '*71' or '*72' (Verizon-style call forwarding codes) are refused while roaming without IMS voice.
findings.risk: None for emergency, TTY, RTT or WPS calls. Emergency numbers reach the check as digit strings (after convertToEmergencyNumber, 1225-1232) and none starts with '*7'. WPS calls start with '*272', '*31#*272' or '#31#*272' (PhoneNumberUtils.java:117-123), which do not start with '*71' or '*72'. TTY relay and RTT calls use ordinary numbers. The only change is that a roaming user without IMS voice cannot dial a '*71'/'*72' forwarding code, which the carrier intends. Note: the key itself is not safe for every value (see key-call_forwarding_blocks_while_roaming_string_array.json).

notes: Proceed. The value blocks only '*71'/'*72' forwarding codes while roaming without IMS voice. The check runs on the emergency dial path too, but no emergency number, WPS prefix or TTY/RTT number can start with these prefixes. The basis is the AOSP Verizon/Xfinity carrier config and Google's CarrierSettings for Verizon-network operators. Read on the LineageOS 23.2 tree; this path has not changed in years, so 24.0 should read the same.
